slides.heading: Min Height Bst
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Search Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Min Height Bst, a medium binary search trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Build a BST of minimal height from a sorted list of distinct ints (pick middle as root).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Build a BST of minimal height from a sorted list of distinct ints (pick middle as root).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Choosing the middle element as the root keeps both halves balanced.
slides.narration: Choosing the middle element as the root keeps both halves balanced.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Insert in sorted order → a linked-list-shaped tree, height n
Insert values one by one in a smart order → O(n log n)
Build directly from midpoints → O(n), height ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉
slides.narration: Inserting sorted values one at a time creates a chain of height n. Picking the middle element as the root and recursing on each half yields minimum height, and building nodes directly takes linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Take the middle of the sorted range as the root
slides.narration: Step by step. First, take the middle of the sorted range as the root. Second, recurse on the left half. Third, recurse on the right half.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Build takes a low and high index. If the range is empty it returns null. Otherwise it creates a node from the middle value and recursively builds its left from the lower half and its right from the upper half.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Build nodes directly; don't call insert (O(n log n))
slides.narration: With an even range, either middle is fine. Creating nodes directly instead of calling insert keeps it linear.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: sorted linked list → BST in O(n)
slides.narration: A good follow-up converts a sorted linked list into a balanced BST in linear time by building in in-order.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Choosing the middle element as the root keeps both halves balanced.
slides.narration: To recap Min Height Bst: Choosing the middle element as the root keeps both halves balanced. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
